questions.stem: Which of the following is the most important and widely cultivated staple food crop in India, officially feeding more than half of the Indian population?
questions.explanation: Rice is the staple food crop of a majority of the people in India. Our country is the second-largest producer of rice in the world after China. It is a kharif crop requiring high temperature and high humidity.

questions.stem: Which specific state in India is currently the largest overall producer of wheat, significantly contributing to the nation's food security?
questions.explanation: While Punjab and Haryana have very high yields per hectare, Uttar Pradesh is the largest producer of wheat in India simply due to the massive land area dedicated to its cultivation in the state.

questions.stem: Which Indian state is traditionally known worldwide as the 'Spice Garden of India' due to its extensive historic production of spices like cardamom, pepper, and cloves?
questions.explanation: Kerala has been a major spice export hub since ancient times (drawing Arab, Portuguese, and Dutch traders). Its tropical climate and hilly terrain (Western Ghats) are perfectly suited for growing a variety of spices.

questions.stem: The term 'Golden Fiber' is popularly used in Indian agriculture and commerce to specifically refer to which important cash crop?
questions.explanation: Jute is known as the golden fiber due to its golden color and its high cash value. It grows well on well-drained fertile soils in the flood plains, primarily in West Bengal, Bihar, and Assam.

questions.stem: Which Indian state is historically the leading producer of soybeans, often officially referred to as the 'Soyabean State' of India?
questions.explanation: Madhya Pradesh has traditionally been the largest producer of soybean in India, often accounting for nearly half of the country's total production, though Maharashtra has recently become a very close competitor.
